name: Tufted vetch
grown_as: A native wild flower of hedges, field edges and rough grassland, perennial
habit: A scrambling, climbing perennial 1 to 2 m, clambering through grass and hedges by branched tendrils. Stems thin, angled, slightly downy. Dies down to the ground in winter.

leaf.type: Compound, pinnate: 6 to 15 pairs of leaflets, the central stalk ending in a branched tendril
leaf.leaflets: Many pairs, unstalked, close-set along the stalk, symmetrical
leaf.outline: Each leaflet narrow, oblong to lance-shaped, 1 to 2.5 cm by 2 to 5 mm
leaf.tip: Blunt or pointed, ending in a tiny bristle point
leaf.stalk: Very short; small, narrow, half arrow-shaped untoothed stipules at its base

flower.form: Small pea flowers packed into a long dense one-sided spike
flower.petals: Five: standard, wings and keel, each flower narrow and pointing down
flower.carried: 10 to 40 flowers in a dense spike 2 to 10 cm, all on one side of the stalk and hanging down; the spike on a long stalk from the leaf joint, about as long as the leaf

fruit: Flat hairless pods 1 to 2.5 cm, green turning brown, each with 2 to 6 small round dark seeds 2 to 3 mm
seedling: The seed leaves stay underground. The first leaves have a few pairs of narrow leaflets and a simple tendril.
winter: Dies back: dead brown stems tangled in the grass, new shoots from the roots in spring

leaf: a branched tendril at the tip
bloom: a dense one-sided spike of small bluish-violet pea flowers
flowers hanging down from one side of the stalk
seed: a small round seed, 2 to 3 mm
seedling: a thin shoot with a few pairs of narrow leaflets
a simple tendril at the leaf tip
young: a scrambling stem with many-leafleted leaves
branched tendrils gripping grass and stems
flower: dense one-sided spikes of bluish-violet flowers
spikes on long stalks from the leaf joints
a tangle of fine pinnate leaves
seedhead: small flat brown pods, 1 to 2.5 cm
pods on the old flower stalks
dormant: dead brown stems lying in grass

look_alikes: Bush vetch (Vicia sepium) has fewer, broader leaflets and only 2 to 6 dull purple flowers in a short cluster. Common vetch (V. sativa) has 1 or 2 pink-purple flowers in the leaf joints. Fodder vetch (V. villosa) has longer flowers with a pouched calyx base.
